rationale: Where the connection to James 2:14-26 states the claim-versus-deed structure Matthew 7:21 shares with James, this connection states the other half of the same underlying tension this lesson's Positions section reports across traditions: Ephesians 2:8-10 states in one short unit both that salvation is "not by works, so that no one can boast" (2:9, BSB) and that believers are "created in Christ Jesus to do good works, which God prepared in advance as our way of life" (2:10, BSB) -- checked directly against this app's own shipped BSB text. Matthew 7:21-23 states a consequence for not "doing the will of My Father" (7:21, BSB) without itself stating whether that doing is the ground of entering the kingdom or the evidence of a prior, freely given standing; Ephesians 2:8-10 is the sharper NT statement of exactly that distinction (grace received apart from works; good works that follow it), which is why this lesson's Positions section cites it rather than treating it as a restatement of the James 2 connection. Graded doctrinal_synthesis rather than parallel because the connection is between two authors' respective teachings on how grace, faith, and works relate to each other, not a shared image or scene; strong rather than explicit because no citation formula links the two texts, though the conceptual precision of Ephesians 2:8-10 on this exact question is substantial and checkable.
